entries.name: Multi-device design
entries.definition: Designing a product's interface so it works well across different devices and screen sizes, such as phones, tablets and desktops.

entries.name: Multi-touch
entries.definition: A touch-input technology that detects two or more simultaneous points of contact, enabling gestures such as pinch and swipe.

entries.name: Multichannel marketing
entries.definition: Marketing to customers through several channels, such as email, social media, stores and websites, at the same time.

entries.name: Multicultural education
entries.definition: An approach to teaching that reflects the histories, cultures and perspectives of diverse groups so that all students have a fair chance to learn.

entries.name: Multitenancy
entries.definition: A software architecture in which one running instance of an application serves several customers, called tenants, whose data is kept separate.

entries.name: Music instruction
entries.definition: Teaching others to play an instrument, sing or understand music.

entries.name: Music theory
entries.definition: The study of how music is built, including notation, scales, harmony, rhythm and form.

entries.name: Mutual exclusion
entries.definition: A requirement in concurrent programming that only one thread or process at a time may use a shared resource or critical section.

entries.name: Mutual funds
entries.definition: Investment vehicles that pool money from many investors to buy a diversified portfolio of securities.

entries.name: Nagle's algorithm
entries.definition: A TCP technique that reduces the number of small packets sent by holding back small writes until earlier data has been acknowledged.

entries.name: Naive Bayes
entries.definition: A family of simple probabilistic classifiers that apply Bayes' theorem while assuming that features are independent of each other given the class.

entries.name: Naked short selling
entries.definition: Selling shares short without first borrowing them or arranging to borrow them, a practice restricted in many markets.

entries.name: NameNode
entries.definition: The master server of the Hadoop Distributed File System, which keeps the file-system namespace and records where each data block is stored.

entries.name: Nanobiotechnology
entries.definition: The field that applies nanoscale technologies to biology and medicine, for example in drug delivery and diagnostics.

entries.name: Nanocomposites
entries.definition: Materials that combine a bulk matrix with particles or fibres smaller than about 100 nanometres to improve properties such as strength or conductivity.

entries.name: Nanolithography
entries.definition: Techniques for printing or etching patterns with features measured in nanometres, used mainly to make semiconductor chips.

entries.name: Nasotracheal suctioning
entries.definition: Clearing secretions from a patient's airway by passing a suction catheter through the nose into the throat and trachea.

entries.name: National Airspace System
entries.definition: The network of United States airspace, airports, navigation facilities, rules and personnel that makes up civil and military flying.

entries.name: National Geothermal Data System
entries.definition: A United States Department of Energy-funded network of geothermal data sources that can be searched together.

entries.name: Nationwide Multistate Licensing System
entries.definition: The online system, run by the State Regulatory Registry, through which US mortgage loan originators and other financial professionals are licensed and registered by state regulators.

entries.name: Native American studies
entries.definition: An interdisciplinary academic field that studies the histories, cultures, politics and societies of Native American peoples.

entries.name: NativeScript
entries.definition: An open-source framework for building native iOS and Android apps from a single JavaScript or TypeScript code base.

entries.name: Natural capital
entries.definition: The world's stock of natural assets, such as land, water, air and living things, that provides goods and services to people.

entries.name: Natural gas pipelines
entries.definition: The pipeline systems that transport natural gas, and the engineering, operation and regulation of them.

entries.name: Natural language generation
entries.definition: The part of natural language processing concerned with having software produce readable human language from data or meaning.

entries.name: Natural language processing
entries.definition: Computational analysis and generation of human language.

entries.name: Natural language processing systems
entries.definition: Software systems that analyse or produce human language, such as translators, chatbots and text classifiers.

entries.name: Natural language understanding
entries.definition: The part of natural language processing concerned with getting machines to grasp the meaning and intent of human language.

entries.name: Nautical charts
entries.definition: Maps made for marine navigation that show water depths, coastlines, hazards and aids to navigation.

entries.name: Navigational aid
entries.definition: A device, marker or system, such as a buoy, beacon or radio transmitter, that helps ships or aircraft find their position and route.

entries.name: Navisworks
entries.definition: Autodesk software that combines design and construction models of a building project so they can be reviewed and checked for clashes.

entries.name: NedGraphics
entries.definition: Computer-aided design software for textile and fashion design, such as print, weave and knit design.

entries.name: Needle localization
entries.definition: Marking the location of a lesion, usually in the breast, by placing a needle or wire under imaging guidance so a surgeon can find and remove it.

entries.name: Neonatal intensive care nursing
entries.definition: Nursing care for critically ill or premature newborns in a neonatal intensive care unit.

entries.name: .NET development
entries.definition: Building software applications on Microsoft's .NET platform, using languages such as C#.

entries.name: Net Promoter Score
entries.definition: A customer loyalty metric based on how likely customers are to recommend a company, scored from -100 to 100.

entries.name: Net zero
entries.definition: A state in which the greenhouse gases a person, company or country puts into the atmosphere are balanced by those removed.

entries.name: Nette
entries.definition: An open-source PHP framework for building web applications.

entries.name: Network intrusion detection system
entries.definition: A tool that monitors network traffic for signs of attacks or policy violations and raises alerts.

entries.name: Network peering
entries.definition: An arrangement in which two networks connect directly to exchange traffic between their own customers, usually without paying each other for transit.
